rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round raises overall obfuscation pressure while protecting IntMM's hot numeric core. SUB is near-free at runtime and size, so it gets the highest SecurityGain weight to transform every function's arithmetic broadly. BCF and FLA carry the biggest runtime penalties and this benchmark's runtime is dominated by tight loops in Intmm and Innerproduct, so their RuntimeCost weights stay high (0.75/0.80) to steer them away from hot-loop functions while still permitting application where features indicate low loop intensity; CorrectnessRisk is nudged up from a trivial baseline because bogus predicates and control-flow flattening are the passes most likely to perturb loop-carried semantics. IBR keeps a moderate runtime weight (0.55) so block-randomization lands mostly on cold functions like Initmatrix, main, and _start. ICALL is pushed up (SecurityGain 0.70) to convert direct calls into indirect dispatches — cheap on a 7-function binary and highly disruptive to static call-graph recovery — with a moderate runtime cost weight reflecting the single extra indirection per call. IGV is favored (RuntimeCost 0.25) since global variable encoding is nearly free here and the program's matrix state is accessed through a small set of globals, giving good resistance per byte of overhead. SPLIT remains a low-cost diversity booster across all functions. Net effect: aggressive arithmetic and call-graph obfuscation everywhere, control-flow-heavy passes gated away from the two hot loops, and total size overhead bounded since the binary starts at only 1312 text bytes.
